full_judgment:
8. Mr. Abdul Mannan Khan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the judgment of the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal in as much as it has not taken into account the evidence relied upon by the trial court and it has also failed to reverse the findings of fact given by the trial court on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 9. I have gone through the judgments of the courts below. As regards the question of title, the trial court has considered the evidence of the 4 P.W s. and also the evidence adduced by the D.Ws. and the documentary evidence and came to the finding that the plaintiffs kabala, Ext. A, is a fraudulent document. The appellate court without considering those evidence and facts and circumstances has given a finding that the kabala Ext. A is genuine and tre plaintiff has been able to prove his title to the suitland. Secondly, the trial court has found that the R.O.R. was published as early as in 1960, but the plaintiff filed the suit some time in the month of March, 1976, long after the registration of the kabala and the plaintiff has failed to give any satisfactory explanation as to why he failed to know about the R.O.R. at the time of the purchase. The plaintiffs vendor Bancharam Kaiborta did not file any suit for correction of the R.O.R. within a period of 3 years R.O.R. at the time of the purchase. The plaintiffs vendor Bancharam Kaiborta did not file any suit for correction of the R.O.R. within a period of 3 years from its final publication. Without considering above facts, the appellate court has abruptly given its finding that the suit is not barred by limitation. So I find substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and hold that judgment of the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal and as such it is liable to be set aside.
